title: Throughput drift timeline and experiments (scratchpad)
content:
Objective: capture a compact timeline of the throughput regression that started 2026-01-14, record quick commands, triage steps, and hypotheses to avoid re-running expensive experiments. This is a personal scratchpad — messy notes, heuristics, and TODOs.

Summary/observed symptoms:
- Starting ~2026-01-14 10:20 UTC our 8-GPU Dedicated pool (p-8a) noticed a steady drop in tokens/sec for short-chat workloads (~20–40 token responses).
- CPU utilization on host nodes unchanged; GPU SM utilization dropped from median 78% -> 42%.
- Latency p50 rose slightly (~5%) but p95/p99 spiked intermittently.
- No config rollouts in Console for model routes at ~10:15 UTC; but a control-plane deploy (autoscaler tweak) happened ~09:50 UTC per release-engineering notes.

Quick timeline (local notes):
- 2026-01-14 09:41 — Canary autoscaler change queued (operator: ops-release).
- 2026-01-14 10:17 — Alerts: throughput drop on prod-dedicated-us-west.
- 2026-01-14 10:23 — First mitigation: scale-out to extra GPU nodes (temporary burst). Throughput restored by ~60% but inconsistent.
- 2026-01-15 — KV cache hit ratio decreased by ~12% for short-prefix workloads (from 0.71 -> 0.59).
- 2026-01-20 — Canary rollback of autoscaler; regression persisted.

What I've checked so far (commands & outputs, trimmed):
- collation of perf metrics (tokens/sec per model, aggregated):
  - sakai@ops:~$ curl -s "https://observability/api/metrics?query=tokens_per_sec%7Bpool%3D%22p-8a%22%7D" | jq '.data'
    => time-series shows step-decline starting 2026-01-14 10:20 UTC.

- node-level containers, looking for throttling / cgroup events:
  - sudo journalctl -u runtime-worker -o short-precise --since "2026-01-14 09:30" | rg -i "throttle|oom|error"
    => no throttles/ooms.

- GPU metrics via nvidia-smi sampling (light):
  - nvidia-smi dmon -s u --delay 2
    => SM% drop aligns with throughput drop. Memory usage stable.

- Traced a single request path with tracing-id X-1K: KV cache lookup present but misses increased. Snapshot of trace indicates more frequent cache invalidations.

Important log snippets (redacted):
- [2026-01-14T10:19:58Z] batch-window: adjusted batch cut-off from 10ms -> 25ms (component: runtime-scheduler)
- [2026-01-14T10:19:59Z] kv-cache: evict-policy switched from LRU to TTL-based for compatibility with new memstore plugin

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Config drift in scheduler + cache policy: The batch-window increase combined with TTL evictions reduced effective batching density for short requests, causing more kernel launches at lower utilization.
2) Incompatibility between new memstore plugin and KV cache resulting in higher miss rates (more KV fetches serialized on host).
3) Downstream I/O latency somewhere (disk or network) introduced extra blocking for small requests, reducing throughput but not showing as OOM or CPU pressure.

Quick experiments to run (cheap first):
- Reproduce locally with a scaled-down harness: replicate 12k QPS of short (10–40 token) requests and toggle batch-window 10ms/25ms and observe tokens/sec and batch-size distribution.
  - Commands: run harness with --sampling=1s and export batch histograms.
- Roll back kv-cache eviction policy on a canary node (one worker) and compare kv hit-rate.
  - Steps:
    1) patch runtime-config: kv_cache.eviction_policy = "lru" on canary
    2) restart worker (graceful), monitor hits via /internal/kv_metrics
- Instrument scheduler to emit per-batch effective_kv_hits metric (quick patch) — will help link cache misses to smaller batch sizes.

Observed micro-behavior from a short-run (2026-01-16 test):
- When batch-window = 25ms median batch size dropped from 8 -> 3 for 10-token traffic (unexpected; thought it would increase).
- Trace shows many requests starting close together but being dispatched across different worker shards (possible sharding skew).

Notes on possible root cause mechanisms (thinking aloud):
- Increasing batch-window alone should increase batch size in steady Poisson traffic, but if a TTL eviction policy aggressively clears long-lived prefixes, batches touching distinct prefixes may be de-densified.
- If memstore plugin serializes access per-prefix and TTL eviction triggers more backend I/O, the scheduler may prefer earlier micro-batches to avoid head-of-line blocking on a single request — resulting in many small batches.
- Shard placement algorithm change: if an earlier deploy changed request routing shard key, request affinity to warm caches may break. Check recent PRs that touched routing (GH-PR-4521 referenced above).

Metrics to gather next (high priority):
- Per-request prefix id distribution (to see if higher cardinality since 2026-01-14).
- Batch-size histogram heatmap over time (1m buckets).
- KV cache hit/miss breakdown by prefix and by worker shard.
- System calls profile (strace-ish) on hot worker during load: look for network/disk syscalls latency.

Short-term mitigations to try (ordered by risk):
- Canary rollback of KV eviction policy on 4 workers (low-risk config flip).
- Reduce batch-window back to 10ms for affected model route (config toggle, low-risk but watch latency).
- Route short-chat traffic to alternate pool (burst) while we triage (requires routing change in Console).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Was any memstore plugin change rolled out ~2026-01-14? (Ops notes mention a plugin rollout but no clear mapping).
- Did any routing shard key change land in GH-PR-4521? Need PR review.
- Are there correlated customer-side patterns (e.g., different prompt shapes) that would increase prefix cardinality?

Quick links and references (local):
- perf-dashboard: https://observability/dashboards/throughput-drift-p8a
- trace example id: X-1K (link: https://tracing/trace/X-1K)
- PR to check: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
- JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3312

TODO (personal):
- [ ] Reproduce locally with harness and capture batch histograms (due: 2026-02-22).
- [ ] Patch scheduler to emit kv_hit_per_batch metric (spike: low-effort, due: 2026-02-25).
- [ ] Ask ops for exact memstore plugin rollout time and binaries (message ops-release).
- [ ] If canary rollback improves hit-rate, draft postmortem outline and mitigation plan.

Extra ephemeral notes (dump):
- Weird: when I force single-shard routing for short requests in test harness, batching density returns to expected levels. Suggests routing-affinity issue.
- If we do reduce batch-window, watch p99 for regression on longer requests; we must avoid regressing latency SLOs while fixing throughput.

End of scratchpad. Keep this file small and ephemeral; will transfer to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime if it stabilizes into an incident write-up.
